title: Year-End Change Approval Checker | What It Routes To
content:
Year-End Change

Year-End Change Approval Checker

A year-end change needing approval is filed elsewhere. Three answers show whether yours is a nil return or a referral.

Three answersCovers a first year-endSays when it is a referralNo rates

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your fiscal year-end

Answer the questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What This Checker Actually Decides

It decides where your return is filed, not whether a year-end change is a good idea. There is one case in which a change takes a corporation outside nil filing: where the change still needs the Canada Revenue Agency to approve it. That case goes to our sister office instead.

Every other answer leaves you with ordinary tax years. A first year-end is chosen rather than approved, an unchanged year-end raises nothing, and a change already approved simply leaves two periods to file.

The Four Answers Side by Side

Your situationApprovalWhat you file
First tax yearNot applicableOne return, on a year-end you choose, capped at 53 weeks
Year-end unchangedNot applicableOne return per year on the same date
Change already approvedSettledTwo periods, two returns, two deadlines, the fee on each
Change still needing approvalOutstandingFiled by our sister office rather than here

The year-end change impact calculator dates the periods a change creates once it is settled, and the fiscal period length calculator measures one against the 53-week limit.

The One Limit on a First Year-End

A first tax year cannot exceed 53 weeks. That is a length limit rather than an approval step, and it is the only constraint on the first year-end a corporation picks.

It still catches people, because a year-end chosen for tidiness can sit more than 53 weeks after the incorporation date. Where it does, the first period has to end earlier and a second period picks up the rest.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does changing a fiscal year-end need CRA approval?

Some changes do. Where a change needs the Canada Revenue Agency to approve it, the filing is outside this service and we route you to our sister office at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year. Where the change is already settled, the periods it created are ordinary tax years and a quiet one is an ordinary nil return.

Does a year-end change mean two returns?

Yes. The old year-end closes one tax year and the new one opens the next, so there are two periods, each with its own return and its own deadline six months after it ends. Each carries $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Can I choose any year-end for a first return?

Any date, with one limit: the first tax year cannot exceed 53 weeks. The year-end also has to match the record the Canada Revenue Agency holds, or the transmission is rejected.

title: T2 Short Exclusion Checker | Which Condition Excludes You
content:
The Short Return

T2 Short Exclusion Checker

The eight T2 Short conditions, and which of them excludes your corporation. Naming the condition is the useful part.

All eight conditionsNames the condition that excludes youSays what each one meansSame fee either way

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

The eight conditions

Answer all eight conditions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

This Page Answers the No, Not the Yes

There are two questions about the T2 Short and they want different pages. Whether a corporation qualifies is a yes or a no, and the T2 Short eligibility checker answers it. Which condition excluded it is a different answer, and that is this page.

Your questionThe page
Can this corporation use the short return?T2 Short eligibility checker
Which condition is stopping it, and what does that condition mean?This page
Short return or full return, and what changes?Nil return vs full return checker

Seven of Eight Is a No

The eight conditions are not weighted and there is no substantial compliance in them. Every one has to hold, so a corporation that meets seven files the full T2.

That is a smaller problem than it sounds. The full T2 is the longer form, not the dearer service: we file whichever one the corporation qualifies for, and both sit inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Two Conditions Reach Past the Form

Two of the eight say something about the year as well as the form. A corporation that is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation, and a corporation that paid or received a taxable dividend, are both outside nil filing here, not merely outside the short return.

Where your answer missed either of those, the result says so. The nil T2 eligibility checker is the page for that question on its own.

Frequently Asked Questions

What excludes a corporation from the T2 Short?

Failing any one of the eight conditions. The conditions are not weighted and there is no partial compliance, so a corporation that meets seven files the full T2 instead.

Does the full T2 cost more than the short return?

No. $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers either one. The short return is a shorter form for a corporation that qualifies, not a cheaper service.

Which conditions also affect whether the year is nil?

Two of them. A corporation that is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation, and one that paid or received a taxable dividend, are outside nil filing here as well as outside the short return. We route those to gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

title: CCPC Condition Checker | The First T2 Short Condition
content:
CCPC Status

T2 Short CCPC Condition Checker

CCPC status decides the first T2 Short condition and whether the year is nil here at all. Four answers settle it.

Four answersDecides a T2 Short conditionDecides nil eligibility tooStatus is held all year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Control and residence

Answer all four questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

One Status, Two Consequences

CCPC status is the first of the eight conditions for the two-page T2 Short. It is also one of the cases that decides whether a corporation is filed here at all: a corporation that is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation goes to our sister office rather than through this service.

If the corporation is a CCPCIf it is not
First T2 Short condition metFirst condition failed, so the full T2 is the return
A quiet year is a nil return at $300.00 plus HST per tax yearFiled by our sister office at $350.00 plus HST per year
The other seven conditions still applyThe other seven stop mattering for the short return

Throughout the Tax Year, Not on One Date

The condition is held throughout the tax year. A corporation that was a CCPC in January and not in November did not meet it for that year, even though it would read as one on either date taken alone.

Which is why a share issue, a change of control or a listing part-way through a year is worth checking against the whole period rather than against the year-end.

What These Four Questions Are Not

They are the four that decide the point for the short return and for nil filing. CCPC status carries other consequences in corporate tax, and those turn on rates and limits this page does not carry and does not guess at.

For the whole eight-condition set, the T2 Short eligibility checker asks them all, and the T2 Short exclusion checker names whichever one excludes you.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does CCPC status appear on a nil filing site?

Because it decides two things at once. It is the first of the eight T2 Short conditions, and a corporation that is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation is outside nil filing here and routes to gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Does the status have to hold all year?

Yes, throughout the tax year. A corporation that held the status for part of the year did not meet the condition for that year.

What if the corporation is not a CCPC?

The full T2 is the return rather than the short one, and the filing is one we route to our sister office. This tool gives general information and is not a filed return.

title: Dissolution Timeline Calculator | The Order and the Dates
content:
Winding Up

Dissolution Timeline Calculator

A dissolution date gives the final T2 deadline and the order of the steps around it, including the ones outside the fee.

Computed final T2 datePuts the steps in orderNames what is outside the feeCovers outstanding years

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your wind-up

Enter the planned dissolution date and answer the question.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Order Is the Useful Part

A wind-up has four steps and only one of them is a date on a form. Getting them in the wrong order is what stalls a dissolution, because two of the four depend on the ones before them.

Unfiled years block a clearance certificate, and they block the dissolution itself. So the outstanding years go first, the final T2 follows, the clearance request comes after the returns are assessed, and the registry filing is last.

Which Steps Are Ours

StepInside $300.00 plus HST per tax year
Each outstanding nil yearYes, at the fee per tax year
The final T2, where the last period is nilYes, at the fee
The clearance certificate requestNo
The registry dissolution filingNo
Closing a GST/HST or payroll accountNo

The dissolution readiness checker tests whether the corporation is ready to start, and the clearance certificate requirement checker covers the third step on its own.

Filing the Final Return Does Not Dissolve It

The final T2 closes the tax record. It does not close the corporation, which stays in existence on the register until the registry dissolution is filed and accepted.

Those are two trails and they end separately. A corporation whose returns are all filed and whose registry record is untouched is still live, and still accruing a filing obligation each year.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the final T2 due?

Within six months of the date of dissolution. The final tax year ends on that date, and the six-month rule runs from it exactly as it does from an ordinary year-end.

Do unfiled years have to be cleared first?

Yes. They block a clearance certificate and they block the dissolution itself, so they are filed before the final return is assessed. Each one is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Does filing the final return dissolve the corporation?

No. The dissolution is a separate registry filing, made with the registry the corporation was incorporated under, and it is not covered by the fee.

title: Payroll Account Closure Checker | RC145 and What Comes First
content:
CRA Accounts

Payroll Account Closure Checker

An open payroll account outlives the payroll. What it still expects, and what Form RC145 closes.

Four answersNames Form RC145An inactive T2 closes nothingSays what is outside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your payroll account

Answer the questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Account Outlives the Payroll

A payroll account is opened once and then stays open. It does not lapse when the last employee leaves, and it does not notice that the corporation went quiet.

So a corporation with no employees and an open account is in the position that surprises people most: nothing to report and a filing still expected. An inactive T2 does not close those accounts.

Three Filings, Three Places

FilingWhat it answers forInside $300.00 plus HST per tax year
The T2Corporate income tax for the yearYes, where the year is nil
A nil payroll remittance or T4The payroll account, while it is openNo
Form RC145Closing the accountNo

The payroll nil remittance checker covers the second row and the CRA account closure sequencer puts the closures in order where there is more than one account.

Outstanding Filings Come Before the Closure

Form RC145 closes an account. It does not forgive what the account was waiting for, so outstanding T4s and outstanding remittances are made first and the closure follows.

Closing in the other order leaves filings outstanding against a closed account, which is a worse position to be in than an open account with nothing owing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does filing a nil T2 close a payroll account?

No. An inactive T2 does not close those accounts. Form RC145 closes a payroll or GST/HST account, it is filed separately, and it is not covered by the fee.

Does an open payroll account need filings with no employees?

While the account is open it goes on expecting returns, whether or not anyone was paid. Closing it with Form RC145 is what stops that.

What has to happen before the account is closed?

Outstanding T4s and outstanding remittances are made first. Form RC145 closes the account; it does not clear what the account was waiting for.

title: Shareholder Register Checker | What Schedule 50 Needs
content:
Schedule 50

Shareholder Register Completeness Checker

Schedule 50 names every shareholder at 10 per cent or more. Four answers show whether your register can fill it.

Four answersThe 10 per cent thresholdNames what each row needsInside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your shareholder register

Answer all four questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Nil Year Still Names Them

Schedule 50 is required for every shareholder holding 10 per cent or more. It is a list of people rather than a set of figures, so a year of zeros does not empty it: the shareholders held their shares throughout the quiet year exactly as they would in a busy one.

Which is the part that catches dormant corporations. The financial schedules may be all zeros while Schedule 50 is as full as it has ever been.

What One Row Needs

For each shareholder at 10 per cent or moreWhere it usually sits
Full legal nameThe share register in the minute book
AddressThe share register, or the annual registry filing
Percentage heldThe share issuance records
Whether the holding crosses 10 per cent at allThe issuance records, totalled

The Schedule 50 shareholder threshold checker answers whether a particular holding crosses the threshold. This page answers whether you can fill the schedule once you know who does.

The Register Also Bears on the GIFI Schedules

Share capital on the books is one of the five things that make GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required on a return that would otherwise omit them. A register that shows issued shares is a register that shows share capital.

So the same records answer two questions. The share capital reporting checker covers the GIFI side.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who has to appear on Schedule 50?

Every shareholder holding 10 per cent or more. The threshold is a floor rather than a limit on the number of rows, so a corporation with six holders above it names six.

Does a nil return still need Schedule 50?

Yes. It reports who holds the shares, not what the corporation earned, so a year of zeros does not empty it.

Is Schedule 50 charged separately?

No. Every schedule a nil return carries sits inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

title: Due To vs Due From Shareholder | Which Side It Sits On
content:
Shareholder Balances

Due To Versus Due From Shareholder

A shareholder balance can run either way. Which direction it is, and why either one makes the GIFI schedules required.

Two answersBoth directions at once is normalReporting, not tax treatmentNames the other four triggers

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your shareholder balance

Answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Direction Changes the Side, Not the Duty

A shareholder balance runs one of two ways. Money the corporation owes a shareholder is a liability, due to the shareholder. Money a shareholder owes the corporation is an asset, due from the shareholder.

For reporting, the direction decides which side of the balance sheet the figure appears on and nothing more. A balance in either direction is a balance, and that is what makes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required on a return that would otherwise omit them.

The Balance Is One of Five Triggers

On the booksMakes the GIFI schedules required
A shareholder loan, either directionYes
Share capitalYes
CashYes
An incorporation costYes
A bank chargeYes

The shareholder loan balance checker answers whether a balance exists at all, and the nil GIFI balance sheet checker runs the whole set of five.

Two Balances Are Not One Balance

An amount due to a shareholder and an amount due from the same person are two balances. They are reported as two, not netted into whichever is larger, because they arose separately and are owed separately.

That is worth saying because the netted figure is the one people hold in their heads. A corporation that owes a shareholder and is owed by the same shareholder has two entries, even where the difference between them is small.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the direction of a shareholder loan change the schedules?

No. A balance in either direction makes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required. The direction decides which side of the balance sheet it sits on.

Can a balance run both ways at once?

Yes, and it often does. The two are separate balances and are reported separately rather than netted together.

Does this tell me the tax treatment of the loan?

No. The tax treatment turns on statutory periods and a prescribed rate, which this tool does not carry. It answers the reporting question: a balance makes the GIFI schedules required.

title: Arbitrary Assessment Response Checker | What Displaces It
content:
CRA Letters

Arbitrary Assessment Response Checker

An assessment raised on a year nobody filed is displaced by the return for that year. Three answers set the order.

Three answersThe return is the responseCovers other open yearsCarries the full qualification

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

The assessment

Answer the questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Built From the Outside

Where a year goes unfiled, an assessment can be raised for it without the corporation’s figures. It is constructed from what the Canada Revenue Agency can see rather than from the books, which is why the numbers on it can look unrelated to a corporation that did nothing at all.

The response is not an argument about those numbers. It is the return for that year, which is the document the figures were standing in for.

File the Assessed Year, and the Others With It

StepWhy in this order
1. The assessed yearIts return is what the assessed figures give way to
2. Any earlier outstanding yearsA T2 carries figures forward, so the years are assessed in order
3. Any later outstanding yearsEach one is its own return and its own year

The catch-up filing schedule generator lays the years out in order, and the CRA demand to file deadline calculator dates a demand letter where one came first.

What a Nil Year Owes on an Assessed Year

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Which is the practical reason to file rather than wait. The year stays open until its return is in, and the return is the only thing that closes it.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I respond to an assessment for a year I did not file?

By filing the return for that year. The assessment was built without the corporation’s figures, and the return is what those figures give way to.

Should I file the other outstanding years at the same time?

Yes, oldest first. A T2 carries figures forward from the year before it, so the years are assessed in the order they fell due. Each one is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

What does a nil year owe on an assessed year?

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

title: Stub Period Return Checker | A Short Year Is Still a Year
content:
Short Tax Years

Stub Period Return Checker

A fiscal period that ended early is its own tax year with its own return and its own deadline. This dates it.

Computed deadlineCovers a dissolution stubCovers a year-end change stubIts own fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your fiscal period

Answer the questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Short Year Is a Whole Tax Year

A stub period is a fiscal period that ended before the usual year-end came round. It feels like a fragment and it is not: it is a tax year in its own right, with its own return, its own six-month deadline and its own fee.

Which is the fact worth having before the work starts, because a year-end change creates two periods where there was one and both of them are returns.

The Two Things That Create One

CauseWhat the stub period isDeadline
Dissolution part-way through a yearThe final tax year, and its return is the final T2Six months after the dissolution date
A fiscal year-end changeThe period closing the old year-end, with a new period opening after itSix months after it ends

The short tax year deadline calculator dates one of these on its own, and the fiscal period length calculator measures how long it ran.

The Fee Is Per Tax Year, Not Per Twelve Months

$300.00 plus HST per tax year is charged per tax year. A stub period is a tax year, so it carries the fee whether it ran eleven months or three weeks.

That reads as a hard line and it is the honest one: the return is the same return, prepared and reviewed and transmitted the same way, whatever length the period was.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a stub period need its own T2?

Yes. A fiscal period that ended early is a short tax year with its own return and its own deadline six months after it ends.

Does a short period cost less?

No. $300.00 plus HST per tax year is charged per tax year, and a stub period is a tax year. The return is prepared, reviewed and transmitted the same way whatever length the period ran.

What creates a stub period?

Most often a dissolution part-way through a year, which makes the stub the final tax year, or a fiscal year-end change, which closes one period and opens another.

title: Account Standing Checker | Two Records, Two Keepers
content:
Two Trails

CRA Account Standing Checker

A corporation has a tax record and a registry record. Three answers show which one is behind and what brings it current.

Three answersSeparates the two recordsCovers being struckSays which filings are outside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 2, 2026

Your two records

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Records, Kept by Two Bodies

Every corporation has two standing records and they are kept in different places. The corporate tax account sits with the Canada Revenue Agency and is brought current by filing returns. The registry record sits with the registry the corporation was incorporated under and is brought current by filing an annual return.

Neither one reports to the other. A corporation whose returns are all filed can be years behind at the registry, and a corporation in good standing at the registry can have an unfiled year from 2019.

What Each One Answers For

RecordKept byBrought current byInside $300.00 plus HST per tax year
Corporate tax accountCanada Revenue AgencyFiling each outstanding T2Yes, per nil tax year
Registry recordThe incorporating registryFiling the outstanding annual returnNo

The unfiled years checker lists the open tax years, and the annual return versus tax return checker separates the two filings where they are being confused for each other.

Being Struck Does Not Settle the Tax Years

Where a registry strikes a corporation for missed filings, the registry record closes. The tax account does not. An unfiled year that was open before the strike is open after it, because the two records are separate trails and only one of them was touched.

The involuntary dissolution risk checker covers the registry side of that, and the open years remain what they were.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does filing my T2 returns fix my registry standing?

No. The corporate tax account and the registry record are separate trails with separate keepers. Filing returns brings the tax account current; the registry annual return brings the registry record current, and it is not covered by the fee.

Does being struck cancel an unfiled T2?

No. The years that were open before the strike are open after it. The registry closing its record does not close the tax account.

Which of the two does this service file?

The T2. Each outstanding nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. Registry annual returns are filed with the registry and are not covered by the fee, and we tell you which ones you still owe.
